articles.headline: OFAC Designates Canadian Money Services Businesses for Facilitating Iranian Regime's Illicit Financial Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated eight Canada-based money services businesses (MSBs) as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast.' These entities are accused of enabling the Iranian regime, sanctioned entities, and other illicit actors to move assets into and out of Iran through financial and cryptocurrency transactions.

The designated MSBs, operating in Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, and surrounding areas, allegedly facilitate the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets. This network supports international transactions involving Iran, including those linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
This action underscores the U.S. commitment to disrupting Iran's economic lifelines and targeting networks involved in oil smuggling, sanctions evasion, and illicit fund movements.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Sanctions on Cuba, Targeting Key Economic Sectors and Military Support Networks
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a new package of sanctions against Cuba, targeting individuals, organizations, and business networks linked to the Cuban government's military support system and financial activities.

The sanctions, issued under Executive Order 14404, designate eight entities and two individuals, along with five vessels identified as blocked property. These measures aim to restrict financial and logistical networks that Washington alleges support the Cuban government's military establishment and enable individuals associated with the leadership to benefit from opaque offshore business arrangements.

Additionally, OFAC published a determination authorizing the imposition of economic sanctions on foreign individuals and entities operating or having operated in Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors. This expands the basis for targeting foreign persons involved in these sectors.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / The Europe Today

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Indian and Turkish Entities for Supporting Iranian Sanctions Evasion, Issues Alert on False Flags
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has imposed fresh Iran-related sanctions on companies and individuals based in India and Turkey. These designations are part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting those accused of helping Iran circumvent restrictions on its oil exports and aviation sector.

Among the designated entities is Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc, sanctioned for allegedly providing ground-handling and other services to several U.S.-designated Iranian airlines, despite repeated warnings. OFAC also sanctioned an India-based couple and associated companies for their alleged involvement in facilitating Iran's 'shadow fleet' through fraudulent maritime registrations and certifications.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC published an alert to the maritime industry, cautioning businesses against dealing with potentially falsely flagged vessels. The alert highlights the substantial risk of designation or penalties for providing services to ships using false flags to evade U.S. sanctions on Iran.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License, Delays Effectiveness of PDVSA Bond Authorization
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL 5AA), further delaying the effectiveness of the authorization in GL 5 until December 18, 2026.

This amendment means that between October 24, 2019, and December 18, 2026, there is no authorization in effect that licenses against subsection 1(a)(iii) of Executive Order 13835 applicable to the holders of the Petroleos de Venezuela, S.A. (PdVSA) 2020 8.5 percent bond.
As a result, transactions related to the sale or transfer of CITGO shares in connection with the PdVSA 2020 8.5 percent bond are prohibited during this period, unless specifically authorized by OFAC.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Iran-related General License. This update revises existing authorizations related to transactions involving Iran.

The specific details of the amendments were not immediately released, but such changes typically aim to clarify the scope of permissible activities or adjust restrictions in response to evolving policy considerations.
Parties engaging in Iran-related transactions are advised to review the updated General License carefully to ensure ongoing compliance with U.S. sanctions regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entity Supporting North Korean IT Worker Schemes
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for allegedly supporting Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes. These schemes are accused of defrauding U.S. companies and generating revenue for North Korea's weapons and missile programs.

Four individuals were designated pursuant to Executive Order 13687, while the entity and six individuals were designated under Executive Order 13722. This action is part of a broader effort by the United States and its partners to disrupt illicit revenue streams supporting the DPRK government.

The designations build on previous actions targeting DPRK IT worker networks and reflect a coordinated effort with Australia and the European Union to counter North Korea's malicious cyber activities and unlawful DPRK-Russia cooperation.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Designations Related to the Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations related to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). These actions aim to address ongoing issues within the region.

While specific details of the designated individuals or entities were not immediately available, such designations typically target those involved in corruption, human rights abuses, or activities that undermine peace and stability in the DRC.
These designations underscore the U.S. commitment to promoting accountability and good governance in the DRC and may impact individuals and entities operating within or connected to the region.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based AI and cloud networking provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. The settlement was announced by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

The violations stemmed from Extreme Networks' exports of networking equipment, software, and related services to a Russian defense manufacturer, Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), between September 2018 and March 2022. MMZA was deemed a blocked person due to its majority ownership by a designated Russian state-owned company, Almaz-Antey, even though MMZA itself was not directly listed on the SDN List until June 2022.

OFAC determined the violations were egregious but voluntarily self-disclosed. The case highlights the importance of thorough due diligence in acquisitions and oversight of foreign affiliates, as well as the need to look beyond direct screening results when red flags indicate a different end-user.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions and Filing Reports
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has amended 11 of its Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) concerning blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC. This update is part of an ongoing review to ensure published guidance remains current.

The revised FAQs, including numbers 10, 32 through 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, clarify when financial institutions must freeze funds due to a blocked person's interest versus rejecting a prohibited transaction where no blockable interest exists. They also address reporting procedures, the 10-business-day deadline for reporting, required supporting documentation, and annual reporting requirements for blocked property.
These amendments do not create a new sanctions program or add designations but are crucial for compliance teams to ensure correct handling of sanctions hits and accurate reporting to OFAC.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Sanctions Law Center

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes PAIPA Designations and Issues Associated General Licenses

PAIPA targets individuals and entities involved in the theft or misappropriation of U.S. intellectual property. The designations aim to protect American innovation and economic security.

The accompanying General Licenses are expected to provide specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited by these new designations, ensuring that legitimate activities are not unduly impacted.

Businesses involved in international trade, particularly foreign entities acting as importers of record, must assess their current operations and ensure they meet the new CTPAT validation or broker requirements to avoid disruptions.

articles.headline: BIS Extends Suspension of 'Affiliates Rule' Until January 10, 2027
body: The U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has announced an extension of the suspension of its 'Affiliates Rule' until January 10, 2027. The rule, which would expand export control restrictions to cover foreign entities owned 50% or more by parties on the Entity List or Military End-User (MEU) List, was originally set to take effect on November 9, 2026.

This extension, filed for public inspection on November 5, 2026, and scheduled for Federal Register publication on November 9, 2026, is part of an ongoing U.S.-China trade arrangement. The delay provides additional time for companies to prepare for the rule's eventual implementation.

Businesses with international operations, particularly those with sourcing, distribution, or customer connections involving China, should utilize this extended period to finalize ownership-based screening and contingency planning, as the rule's future remains tied to the U.S.-China trade dynamic.

articles.headline: Department of Commerce Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR), rather than the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.
This deregulatory action aims to align export controls on suppressors with the controls already applied to firearms. The change is expected to streamline the export process for these items.
Exporters of sound suppressors should familiarize themselves with the updated regulations under the EAR to ensure compliance with the new control framework.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
body: Millions of Indians are marking the festival of lights with glowing lamps, fireworks and traditional sweets.

articles.headline: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
body: Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, has not commented.

articles.headline: 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years
body: The national mood is low, and faith in politics even lower - with voters deserting the major parties at the polls.

articles.headline: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
body: Santiago Peña was ousted due to a banking crisis which left millions of people unable to access their money.

articles.headline: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
body: Pope Leo travels to Uruguay just three weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

articles.headline: Meghan's father Thomas Markle under house arrest after child sex abuse material charge
body: The 82-year-old appeared in court in Florida after the FBI searched two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented.

articles.headline: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
body: The former Brexit negotiator says EU countries would reject any British attempts to follow economic rules "a la carte".

articles.headline: Texas mayor instructs police to limit co-operation with ICE
body: There has been months of public outcry in Houston after an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer fatally shot a man who was driving to work.

articles.headline: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
body: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.

articles.headline: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
body: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.

articles.headline: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
body: Prosecutors begin investigating EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people.

articles.headline: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
body: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".

articles.headline: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
body: At least seven people died when two trains collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.

articles.headline: How the deadly shooting in Krakow unfolded
body: Video authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment gunshots rang out in Krakow's main market square.

articles.headline: Gaza wedding festival sees 250 couples married at the same time
body: A mass wedding for Palestinian brides and grooms has taken place in the rubble-strewn streets of Gaza.

articles.headline: Watch: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck?
body: The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.

articles.headline: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?
body: Republicans can stick with Trumpism or chart a new path, writes BBC Washington correspondent Daniel Bush.

articles.headline: Germans wrestle with what to do with Hitler's destroyed Eagle's Nest retreat
body: While some believe the site should be partially or completely rebuilt, others want it abandoned and all memory of its Nazi past forgotten.
